name: Sydney Gardens Community Orchard
short_description: Accessible orchard in Sydney Gardens park.
description: Apple, pear and plum trees can be found along the orchard trail within this historic pleasure garden.

name: Widcombe Community Garden
short_description: Shared edible garden open to all.
description: A thriving community garden with raised beds growing seasonal vegetables, salad leaves and herbs. Visitors are welcome to take surplus produce.

name: Incredible Edible Bath (City Centre Planters)
short_description: Edible street planters throughout central Bath.
description: Community-maintained planters near the Guildhall and Parade Gardens growing herbs, edible flowers and leafy greens.

name: Bathampton Meadows Elderberries
short_description: Elder trees along the River Avon towpath.
description: Abundant elder trees line the riverside path between Bathampton and Batheaston. Elderflower in June and berries in September.

name: Prior Park Landscape Garden (Boundary Hedgerows)
short_description: Nut trees along the estate boundary paths.
description: Hazel and walnut trees can be found along the public footpaths bordering the National Trust estate. Access does not require entry to the garden.

name: Smallcombe Wood Hazelnuts
short_description: Hazel coppice in ancient Smallcombe Wood.
description: A beautiful woodland walk with hazel coppice throughout. The nuts are ready to pick in late September and October.

name: Primrose Hill Community Orchard
short_description: Restored heritage orchard in Primrose Hill park.
description: A community-managed orchard with heritage apple and pear varieties. Picking events held in autumn; fruit left on the ground is free to take.

name: Combe Down Wild Plum
short_description: Wild plum and damson trees on the hillside.
description: A scattering of wild plum and damson trees found along the public footpath on the southern slopes of Combe Down village.

name: Kelston Round Hill Sloes
short_description: Blackthorn hedgerows on the Cotswold Way.
description: Dense blackthorn hedges line the Cotswold Way footpath near Kelston Round Hill. Sloes are best picked after the first frost in October.

name: Bath Community Orchard (Broadmoor Lane)
short_description: Established community orchard in south Bath.
description: A community-run orchard with a wide range of apple, cherry and pear trees. Surplus fruit is available for public picking throughout the season.

name: River Avon Path Wild Garlic
short_description: Wild garlic carpets the riverside woodland.
description: The wooded riverbank between Bath and Saltford is blanketed in wild garlic in spring. Best before flowering in April.

name: Cotswold Way Walnuts (North Stoke)
short_description: Walnut trees on the Cotswold Way footpath.
description: Several mature walnut trees grow alongside the Cotswold Way between North Stoke and Wick. Nuts fall from mid-September onwards.

name: Odd Down Allotments Surplus Stall
short_description: Honesty-box surplus veg from local allotments.
description: Local allotment holders put out surplus fruit and vegetables on an honesty-box stall at the site entrance throughout the growing season.

name: Lansdown Hill Blackberries
short_description: Brambles along the open Lansdown hillside.
description: Extensive blackberry brambles grow along the public footpaths and field edges crossing Lansdown hill, north of Bath.

name: Incredible Edible Bath (Green Park Station)
short_description: Edible planters at the old Green Park Station.
description: Seasonal planters outside the former Green Park Station and the adjoining Saturday market grow herbs and edible greens for public picking.
